brief.headline: Berry Global is a 100% trader with distress-zone finances — shift volume to a manufacturer or win a 4.3% price cut plus faster payment against our ₹81.39 L annual spend

priceAsk.summary: Cut price by 4.3% to match the best supplier we already pay, or accept that we will shift volume to a direct manufacturer
priceAsk.target: ₹1.62/NOS on LDPE BOTTLE 5ML WHITE OPAQUE (currently ₹1.69/NOS), saving ₹3.37 L annually
priceAsk.basis: Bprex Pharma Packaging India (P) Limited supplies the same SKU at ₹1.62/NOS — a 4.3% gap. Berry manufactures 0.0% and trades 100.0%, so their price carries a reseller margin we should not pay when a maker is available at ₹1.62/NOS.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Maintain current 30 Days After Receipt terms; do not extend credit to a distressed supplier
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹6.69 L working capital already tied up at 30-day terms

brief.financialLeverage: Berry Global India posted a -199.2% net margin in FY2023-24 (peer median 2.3%), an Altman Z-score of -0.18 (distress zone), and debt-to-equity of 220.44x. Their Probe42 score is 1/10 and they are loss-making. Our ₹81.39 L spend represents 7.21% of their ₹11.29 Cr revenue, so we matter — but their fragility means any hard squeeze risks tipping supply. Lead with qualifying a second source and framing the conversation around continuity, not a brutal price war. Their 335d cash-conversion cycle (peer median 70d) and 2.77% borrowing cost suggest they value speed, but paying them early funds a trader's working capital without capturing the maker's price.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B (65/100) — a robust, direct-manufacturing second source for pharma bottles and caps

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-packaging leader with ₹946.50 Cr revenue and health score A (79/100) — strong, profitable alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Bprex Pharma Packaging India (P) Limited
alternates.why: Already our best-price supplier at ₹1.62/NOS for the same LDPE bottle — credible benchmark and volume-shift target

risks: Berry's Altman Z of -0.18 and -199.2% margin put them in distress — pushing too hard may trigger supply failure before we have volume placed elsewhere
They are 100.0% traded, so any price cut eats into a thin reseller margin rather than manufacturing cost — limited room to move without destroying their economics
Our ₹81.39 L is 7.21% of their revenue, so walking away hurts them, but we have ₹6.69 L of working capital at risk if they collapse mid-contract
Their 220.44x debt-to-equity and negative free cash flow of ₹-164.97 Cr mean refinancing or solvency risk — do not extend payment terms or prepay
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value continuity, but we're paying ₹1.69 when the same bottle is available at ₹1.62 from a manufacturer — help us understand why we should carry a trader margin when we can go direct.
